name: matcher ignores the load state
why: The rel-state-* branch matches every row, so checking "request failed" does not narrow the table — the skill's silently-dead-entry failure mode.
grep: narrows the table to exactly the failed row

name: section never rendered
why: The load-state entries are never added to the dropdown.
grep: lists all four states with their counts

name: zero-count entry shown
why: A fully loaded table still offers a "not loaded yet" entry with a count of 0.

name: collapsed note ignores loaded rows
why: A partly loaded collapsed column still says nothing is loaded.
grep: lists all four states with their counts

name: classifier reports an empty row as having relationships
why: _relCellLoadState() says 'has' for a fetched row with no icon, so the counts merge two different states.
grep: lists all four states with their counts

name: icon counts skipped on a collapsed but partly loaded column
why: A row loaded by hand in a collapsed column has an icon, but the "Relationship icons" section does not list it.
grep: lists all four states with their counts

name: writers do not drop the uniq-drop cache (overlap)
why: KNOWN OVERLAP: the spec loads rows by clicking, and _relLoadRow() drops the table's uniq-drop cache itself after its write, so removing the per-write drop in _relScheduleProgressRefresh() is invisible there. It matters for bulk writes during a fetch, which the spec does not reopen the dropdown during. Recorded, not hidden.
